options.B: The absence of any medical terminology in nursing
options.C: Mandatory laws forbidding nurses from collecting data
options.D: A complete lack of patients in government hospitals

explanation: Too true! Juggling busy ward shifts and direct patient care leaves very little breathing room for extra projects. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T6#GNS217_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which patient will benefit most from a nebulizer instead of a standard inhaler?

options.A: An active athlete who needs a quick rescue puff before playing football
options.B: A severely breathless patient who struggles to coordinate breathing with an inhaler
options.C: A healthy adult who prefers taking their daily maintenance medication quickly
options.D: A patient who experiences dry mouth from using anticholinergic inhalers

explanation: Nebulizers turn liquid medicine into a cool mist that the patient can breathe in easily during normal breathing, making them perfect for someone in severe respiratory distress. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T2#GNS223_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is a common mistake beginners make when trying out a test of change?

options.A: Treating the test as a single, one-time event rather than a series
options.B: Running cycles that are entirely too short to measure
options.C: Collecting too much numerical data from frontline staff
options.D: Involving too many nurses in the initial planning stages

explanation: Improvement is a journey, not a one-off exam! Don't get discouraged if the first try isn't perfect; it's meant to be an ongoing series of small tweaks. [learn more](GST319_U3_T4#GST319_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the relationship between the patient's clinical health record and an internal incident report?

options.A: The incident report is an administrative risk document and is kept separate from the clinical chart
options.B: Both documents are legally identical and stored in the exact same physical folder
options.C: The incident report must be copied word-for-word into the progress notes of the chart
options.D: The clinical chart is kept confidential while the incident report is posted publicly

explanation: Incident reports are administrative tools used for quality improvement and remain separate from the clinical medical record. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h6)

question: What do we call single-ring sugar molecules like glucose and fructose?

options.A: Amino acids
options.B: Monosaccharides
options.C: Polysaccharides
options.D: Triglycerides

explanation: You got it! 'Mono' means single, and 'saccharide' means sugar, making monosaccharides the simplest form of carbohydrate. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h2)

question: Why do nurse researchers use experimental designs instead of simple observation?

options.A: Observation cannot control outside factors that might skew results
options.B: Experiments are much easier to perform on busy wards
options.C: Patients prefer being in experimental groups
options.D: Observation takes too much money and time

explanation: Active control in experiments lets researchers rule out other explanations for patient recovery or change, giving much stronger proof than just watching patients. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which nerve brings the parasympathetic signals that make the bladder contract when you want to pee?

options.A: Pudendal nerve
options.B: Obturator nerve
options.C: Hypogastric nerve
options.D: Pelvic nerve

explanation: Spot on! The pelvic nerve carries those important parasympathetic signals that tell the detrusor muscle to squeeze and empty the bladder. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h2)

question: When a researcher collects 'primary data', what are they doing?

options.A: Records taken from old hospital admission logs from ten years ago
options.B: Data published in international textbooks without any author names
options.C: Information collected directly by the researcher for the current study
options.D: Information guessed by the nurse without asking the patient

explanation: That's correct! Primary data is freshly gathered firsthand by the investigator specifically for their current study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T20#GNS224_U1_T20_h2)

question: Which type of bedpan is best to use for a patient who has a broken hip?

options.A: A standard high-backed bedpan
options.B: A rigid plastic commode chair
options.C: A fracture pan
options.D: A pediatric incontinence ring

explanation: Fracture pans are shallow, meaning you don't have to lift the patient's hips high up. This is a lifesaver for avoiding extra pain or injury when dealing with hip or pelvic bones! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h2)

question: Why is having a clear 'case definition' so important during a disease outbreak?

options.A: It guarantees that the disease will not spread to neighboring towns.
options.B: It automatically cures the patients who fit the diagnostic description.
options.C: It prevents the government from spending money on laboratory testing.
options.D: It ensures all investigators identify and count cases using the exact same criteria.

explanation: Spot on! A clear case definition makes sure every nurse and doctor is looking for the exact same signs, preventing confusion in our records. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T13#GNS313_U1_T13_h5)

question: How can a tele-nurse make sure a patient truly understood instructions given during a video call?

options.A: Ask the patient to repeat the instructions back in their own words.
options.B: Assume understanding if the patient nods once during the video call.
options.C: Send a written legal contract via email for signature.
options.D: Check the patient's medical history for past compliance.

explanation: This is called the 'teach-back' method, and it's a brilliant way to ensure clear communication without making the patient feel tested. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a requirement for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM) to work safely?

options.A: The baby must be exclusively breastfed
options.B: The infant must be older than one year
options.C: The infant must be under six months of age
options.D: The mother must not have resumed menstruation

explanation: LAM is a temporary method that only works for the first six months after birth, as long as breastfeeding is exclusive and periods haven't returned. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T009#GNS226_U6_T009_h5)

question: Why must nurses regularly check the expiration dates of medicines in a clinic pharmacy?

options.A: To decide which nurse gets a promotion
options.B: To prevent patients from receiving expired or ineffective drugs
options.C: To make the medicine shelves look neat and colorful
options.D: To increase the financial profit of the local government

explanation: Expired medications may lose their chemical potency or become toxic, harming the patient instead of curing them. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h9)

question: What is the main job of haustrations (pocket-like folds) in the colon?

options.A: Adding digestive juices to the food mixture
options.B: Speeding up the travel time of liquid waste
options.C: Pushing stool directly out of the anus
options.D: Mixing food contents to help the body absorb water

explanation: Think of haustrations as gentle churning movements in the large intestine. They mix things up slowly so the bowel lining has enough time to soak up water and minerals! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h1)

question: Which symptom experienced immediately after the contrast injection is considered a normal, expected reaction?

options.A: Sudden swelling of the tongue and lips
options.B: Complete inability to speak or move
options.C: Severe shortness of breath and wheezing
options.D: A warm flushing sensation and a salty taste

explanation: Most patients feel a sudden wave of warmth and notice a metallic or salty taste when the dye enters their bloodstream. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is proper waste management in a health facility considered a crucial part of infection control?

options.A: It prevents environmental reservoirs from harboring and spreading pathogens
options.B: It lowers the overall financial cost of purchasing medications
options.C: It guarantees that patients will never develop drug allergies
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for nurses to wash their hands

explanation: Safe disposal of contaminated waste removes potential reservoirs where infectious agents can multiply and reach new hosts. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h7)

question: What is the main goal of the DOTS (Directly Observed Therapy Short-Course) program?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of manufacturing TB drugs
options.B: To eliminate the need for sputum microscopy tests
options.C: To force patients to stay admitted in the hospital for six months
options.D: To ensure patients swallow every dose of medicine to prevent drug resistance

explanation: With DOTS, a health worker watches the patient take their medication. This makes sure they finish the course and stops drug-resistant TB from developing. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which nursing intervention helps prevent caregiver burnout in a home care setting?

options.A: Telling the primary caregiver to work harder and take fewer breaks
options.B: Ignoring family stress to focus exclusively on medical wound care
options.C: Suggesting that the patient move into a nursing home immediately
options.D: Connecting the family with local respite care and adult day programs

explanation: Respite care gives tired caregivers a much-needed break, protecting both their health and the older adult's safety. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T10#GNS324_U3_T10_h6)

question: When do pregnant women most commonly start experiencing symptoms of constipation?

options.A: Early in the first trimester
options.B: Only during active labor
options.C: Right after delivery occurs
options.D: Exclusively in the final week

explanation: Great job! Hormonal shifts happen right from the start of pregnancy, which is why tummy troubles often pop up early in the first trimester. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h1)

question: When washing your hands, what is the minimum time you should scrub with soap?

options.A: Five seconds
options.B: Ten seconds
options.C: One minute
options.D: Twenty seconds

explanation: Great job! Scrubbing for at least 20 seconds is the golden rule to properly lift and wash away germs from your skin. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h2)

question: Why are broad-spectrum antibiotics started immediately instead of waiting for lab results?

options.A: Culture results are always inaccurate during the postpartum period
options.B: Delaying treatment allows the infection to worsen rapidly and threaten life
options.C: Broad-spectrum drugs have no side effects for the nursing mother
options.D: Hospital accreditation standards fine units that delay medication

explanation: Sepsis is a race against time! Waiting days for lab results could let the infection spiral out of control, so we start treatment right away. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h6)

question: What do not-for-profit health organizations do with any extra money they make?

options.A: Transfer it directly to government tax accounts
options.B: Distribute it equally among private shareholders as dividends
options.C: Reinvest it into facility improvement and patient care
options.D: Hold it in offshore bank accounts for future business ventures

explanation: You got it! Not-for-profit centers put every extra naira right back into upgrading their equipment and helping the community. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h4)

question: What is a common cause of latex allergies among healthcare workers?

options.A: Drinking contaminated water from hospital supply pipes
options.B: Touching metal instruments sterilized in chemical baths
options.C: Repeated skin exposure to natural rubber proteins in gloves
options.D: Inhaling powder from standard surgical face masks

explanation: Wearing rubber gloves all day exposes your skin to natural proteins over and over, which can sensitize your immune system and trigger allergies over time. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h3)

question: Which of the following is an example of demographic data found in an EHR?

options.A: Active blood pressure medication list
options.B: Serum potassium lab test results
options.C: Chest X-ray diagnostic imaging report
options.D: Patient home address and phone number

explanation: Demographics refer to basic personal and contact details rather than clinical test results or treatments. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h2)

question: Blood from under the tongue flows directly into which major vein on its way to the heart?

options.A: Renal artery
options.B: Hepatic portal vein
options.C: Femoral vein
options.D: Internal jugular vein

explanation: You've got this! The sublingual veins drain straight into the internal jugular vein to reach the heart quickly. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h2)

question: Two clinical nurses independently score a patient's wound healing using the same chart. What type of reliability are they testing?

options.A: Parallel forms reliability
options.B: Test-retest reliability
options.C: Inter-rater reliability
options.D: Internal consistency reliability

explanation: Since two separate raters are checking their agreement on the same patient, it's inter-rater reliability in action! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h5)

question: Who is the main officer at the Local Government level in charge of gathering disease reports?

options.A: Chief Pharmacist of the Federal Teaching Hospital
options.B: Local Government Area Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer
options.C: National Minister of Finance and Budget Planning
options.D: Director of Immigration and Border Control

explanation: Spot on! The LGA DSNO is the key person coordinating surveillance and collecting initial reports from health facilities in the area. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h5)

question: A patient on chemotherapy has a dangerously low neutrophil count. What is your most critical nursing action?

options.A: Massaging swollen lymph nodes firmly every few hours
options.B: Enforcing strict hand hygiene and restricting sick visitors
options.C: Encouraging fresh, unwashed garden salads
options.D: Administering live polio vaccines

explanation: Low neutrophils mean low infection-fighting power! Hand hygiene and keeping germs away are absolute lifesavers here. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T9#GNS311_U2_T9_h7)

question: Which goal of health spending focuses specifically on making sure poor and vulnerable citizens are not left out?

options.A: Quality assurance
options.B: Cost containment
options.C: Equity
options.D: Privatization

explanation: Think of equity as fairness. It ensures that healthcare resources reach everyone, especially those with lower incomes. [learn more](GST322_U3_T3#GST322_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which feature is most characteristic of a quantitative research study?

options.A: Statistical analysis and measurement
options.B: Detailed personal stories and interviews
options.C: Focus only on historical events
options.D: Absence of any numerical data

explanation: Quantitative research deals with numbers, variables, and measurable outcomes to test hypotheses. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h4)

question: A client wants a method she can insert herself vaginally hours before intercourse to block sperm. Which supply method is this?

options.A: Diaphragm with spermicide
options.B: Emergency hormonal pill
options.C: Combined oral contraceptive pill
options.D: Male latex condom

explanation: A diaphragm is a dome-shaped barrier a woman places inside to cover her cervix, especially when paired with sperm-killing cream. Spot on! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T5#GNS225_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why is it important to understand cultural beliefs during palliative communication?

options.A: It prevents patients from talking about their symptoms
options.B: It allows nurses to change the patient's religious beliefs
options.C: It is required to reduce hospital medication costs
options.D: It helps tailor care discussions to respect family traditions and elders

explanation: Culture shapes how families view illness and make decisions, especially with elders involved. Respecting this makes our nursing care truly compassionate. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T2#GNS321_U4_T2_h6)

question: A newborn has a persistent shunt directing blood from the pulmonary artery to the aorta. What structure failed to manage this normal foetal pathway?

options.A: The foramen ovale
options.B: The ductus arteriosus
options.C: The ductus venosus
options.D: The umbilical vein

explanation: The ductus arteriosus is the specific vessel connecting the pulmonary artery to the aorta during foetal life. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h4)

question: Which activity is a key community prevention strategy for GBV in displacement settings?

options.A: Establishing safe spaces for women and girls
options.B: Banning all public gatherings and educational meetings
options.C: Locking all community members inside their tents at night
options.D: Stopping all clinical treatment services in displacement camps

explanation: Safe spaces give women and girls a secure area to gather, find peer support, and join community empowerment programs. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T11#GNS312_U4_T11_h9)

question: Which specific nerve fibers in the skin are responsible for sending itch signals to the brain?

options.A: Pacinian touch receptors
options.B: Unmyelinated C-fibers
options.C: Meissner corpuscle endings
options.D: Large myelinated A-alpha fibers

explanation: Unmyelinated C-fibers are specialized nerve endings in our skin that pick up itch (pruritic) signals and carry them to the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h4)

question: A patient with a chronic illness stops taking their routine medicines because they can no longer afford cash payments. What is this financial challenge called?

options.A: Over-insurance by the federal scheme
options.B: Mandatory prepayment taxation
options.C: Catastrophic out-of-pocket expenditure
options.D: Excessive foreign donor funding

explanation: Spot on! Paying cash directly for chronic medical care quickly drains family savings, forcing many patients to abandon their treatment. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h3)

question: You see a colleague pouring leftover liquid antibiotics down the hospital sink. What is the right nursing response?

options.A: Help pour the remaining bottles down the drain to finish faster
options.B: Stop the colleague and explain proper pharmaceutical waste disposal
options.C: Throw the empty glass bottles into the general household trash bin
options.D: Ignore the action since liquid drugs dissolve safely in water pipes

explanation: Fantastic clinical judgment! Pouring medications down regular drains pollutes local water systems. Proper disposal protects both our patients and our environment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h7)

question: What happens to infectious soft waste after it successfully goes through an autoclave cycle?

options.A: It becomes radioactive and needs special deep burial.
options.B: It instantly turns into liquid that pours down the drain.
options.C: It is sterilized and can often be handled like general waste.
options.D: It must still be burned in an open outdoor pit.

explanation: You're doing great! Once an autoclave kills all the infectious germs, the treated waste is safe and no longer poses a biological hazard. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h4)

question: At a hot outdoor concert, a nurse notices attendees feeling dizzy, nauseous, and sweating heavily. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Immediately discharge them from the venue without further assessment
options.B: Administer powerful intravenous antibiotics to all affected individuals
options.C: Move them to a shaded cooling area and provide oral rehydration
options.D: Advise them to continue dancing until the concert concludes

explanation: Classic signs of heat exhaustion! Getting them out of the sun and giving fluids right away stops it from turning into heatstroke. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T3#GNS315_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the best first step when you notice an outlier in your research data?

options.A: Ignore it completely because outliers never matter in research
options.B: Investigate it for potential recording errors or unique clinical cases
options.C: Delete the point immediately to make the graph look cleaner
options.D: Change the scale of the axis so the point disappears

explanation: Always check if it's just a typing mistake, or if it's an exciting, unusual patient case worth noting! Don't just delete data blindly. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T12#GNS217_U4_T12_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of regular student evaluation?

options.A: Clearing away all hospital errors forever
options.B: Encouraging steady study habits
options.C: Building your confidence in clinical skills
options.D: Helping you reflect on your own progress

explanation: Evaluations make us much safer, but let's be real—no test can completely wipe out human error in a busy hospital. We're all human! [learn more](GST321_U9_T2#GST321_U9_T2_h4)

question: Which group of professionals makes up the core mental health team?

options.A: Pharmacists, physiotherapists, and laboratory technicians
options.B: Surgeons, anesthetists, and theater nurses
options.C: Psychiatrists, nurses, social workers, and occupational therapists
options.D: Hospital administrators, accountants, and security officers

explanation: Spot on! Good mental health care brings together medical, nursing, social, and daily living expertise. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h5)

question: What is widely known as the biggest challenge facing drug safety systems around the world?

options.A: Underreporting of adverse drug reactions
options.B: Too many digital reporting applications
options.C: Immediate withdrawal of safe medications
options.D: An excess of trained clinical investigators

explanation: Spot on! Many busy clinicians forget or fail to report side effects, meaning most mild or moderate reactions go completely undocumented. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h7)

question: What was the main focus of early psychoanalytic therapy?

options.A: Isolating patients from stressful family environments
options.B: Training patients to change bad habits through rewards
options.C: Exploring hidden conflicts in the unconscious mind
options.D: Using electrical shocks to reset brain chemistry

explanation: Psychoanalysis aimed to bring repressed memories and hidden emotional struggles from the unconscious into conscious awareness. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why do nurses focus so much on controlling the infection reservoir?

options.A: It prevents patients from developing drug allergies
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for handwashing
options.C: It stops the spread of disease at its source
options.D: It cures chronic illnesses in individual patients

explanation: Spot on! When you target the reservoir, you cut off the germs right at their source so they can't spread any further. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h1)

question: What happens if a nurse shakes a vial of reconstituted medication too vigorously?

options.A: The active ingredients in the medication instantly multiply
options.B: The medicine changes color to indicate it is ready
options.C: Excessive foam and bubbles form, making accurate measurement difficult
options.D: The glass vial shatters due to rapid temperature changes

explanation: Vigorous shaking whips air into the liquid, creating foam and bubbles that distort volume measurements inside the syringe. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h5)

question: When do symptoms of neonatal tetanus usually first show up?

options.A: At approximately six months postpartum
options.B: Between three and fourteen days after birth
options.C: Around six to eight weeks of age
options.D: Within the first 24 hours of life

explanation: Spot on! Symptoms typically appear in the first two weeks of life, often after the baby was feeding and acting completely normal at first. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T018#GNS226_U3_T018_h1)

question: What should you do if you are holding a sterile instrument package and suddenly feel unsure if it's truly sterile?

options.A: Use it only if the outer wrapper looks clean
options.B: Consider it contaminated and discard it
options.C: Wipe the instrument down with an antiseptic
options.D: Ask the surgeon to inspect the item before use

explanation: When in doubt, throw it out! Patient safety always comes first, so never take chances with a questionable sterile item. [learn more](GST114_U2_T13#GST114_U2_T13_h3)

question: A community health nurse notices a sudden rush of parents requesting routine check-ups for young girls right before long school holidays. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Families preparing daughters for upcoming FGM ceremonies
options.B: Standard preventive screening recommended by public health
options.C: A sudden regional outbreak of adolescent infections
options.D: Parents seeking routine sports physicals for school teams

explanation: School holidays are prime time when families travel home or arrange for girls to undergo FGM. Always stay alert for these patterns in community practice! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h6)

question: Why do differing goals cause friction in collaborative health projects?

options.A: One partner prioritizes financial return while another prioritizes equity
options.B: It automatically increases patient wait times in private clinics
options.C: It prevents hospitals from purchasing any medications
options.D: It forces all nurses to switch from public to private employment

explanation: When one partner cares mostly about profit and another cares mostly about equal access for everyone, it can be tricky to agree on budgets and pricing. [learn more](GST322_U5_T3#GST322_U5_T3_h7)

question: If the upper (head) end of the neural tube fails to close properly, which organ's development is most affected?

options.A: Kidneys
options.B: Liver
options.C: Heart
options.D: Brain

explanation: Spot on! The top end of the neural tube (the anterior neuropore) forms the head, so proper closure here is essential for normal brain development. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T1#GNS211_U3_T1_h2)

question: Besides blood-borne viruses, what other common infection can result from using non-sterile injection equipment?

options.A: Bacterial infections causing abscesses and sepsis
options.B: Fungal infections affecting the respiratory tract
options.C: Parasitic infections residing in the bloodstream
options.D: Genetic disorders altering red blood cells

explanation: Unsterile equipment introduces bacteria straight into tissues, which can lead to painful local abscesses or severe blood infections like sepsis. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h2)

question: A nurse arrives in a new village to start a malaria project. What should she do FIRST?

options.A: Order the demolition of stagnant water pools near the houses
options.B: Distribute mosquito nets to the first people she meets on the road
options.C: Set up a treatment table in the market square and wait for patients
options.D: Visit the village chief and key community leaders to introduce herself

explanation: Proper community entry requires meeting leadership and building rapport before taking any health action. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which measurement is most important for checking brain growth or fluid buildup in an infant?

options.A: Crown-to-heel length
options.B: Chest circumference
options.C: Mid-upper arm circumference
options.D: Head circumference

explanation: Great! Measuring head circumference routinely helps us monitor brain development and spot any abnormal swelling or fluid early. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T2#GNS225_U3_T2_h5)

question: What is drug tolerance?

options.A: Rapid excretion of medicine by healthy kidneys
options.B: An allergic reaction occurring on first exposure
options.C: A reduced response to a drug after repeated use
options.D: The complete inability of a drug to bind receptors

explanation: Tolerance happens when your body gets too used to a medicine over time, meaning you might need a bit more of it to get the same effect. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T6#GNS125_U1_T6_h7)

question: Why is electrical muscle stimulation sometimes used during physical rehabilitation?

options.A: To permanently replace voluntary muscle contraction
options.B: To help re-educate and stimulate muscles that have lost nerve signaling
options.C: To provide general systemic pain relief like a warm bath
options.D: To rapidly increase red blood cell production

explanation: Spot on! Gentle electrical pulses can help wake up and contract muscles that aren't receiving normal signals from the brain yet. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h5)

question: Why is healthcare treated as a public good that needs government regulation?

options.A: The free market cannot distribute it fairly on its own
options.B: It is completely free to produce in all situations
options.C: Private companies refuse to build any hospitals
options.D: International law forbids selling medicine for profit

explanation: If left completely to market forces, businesses focus only on profit rather than who actually needs medical help. That's why the government steps in! [learn more](GST322_U3_T3#GST322_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why must community health nurses look beyond basic medical treatment to be effective advocates?

options.A: Because clinical treatments are no longer effective in modern hospitals
options.B: Because social and economic conditions heavily influence overall health outcomes
options.C: Because government policies forbid treating patients without community approval
options.D: Because doctors expect nurses to handle administrative tasks

explanation: You got it! Things like poverty, housing, and education shape a person's health just as much as medicine does, so nurses have to look at the whole picture. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h1)

question: If someone has a family history of anxiety, what role does a major life stressor play?

options.A: It only affects physical heart rate and blood pressure
options.B: It can act as a trigger that activates the underlying condition
options.C: It completely erases any chance of developing symptoms
options.D: It replaces the need for biological evaluation entirely

explanation: Think of the genetic tendency as a loaded gun, and severe stress as the trigger that pulls it. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T1#GNS314_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of making a community nursing diagnosis after data collection?

options.A: To replace the need for physical examinations during home health visits
options.B: To diagnose individual rare diseases without consulting a medical doctor
options.C: To punish local authorities for failing to provide proper sanitation facilities
options.D: To clearly identify population health problems and plan targeted interventions

explanation: A community diagnosis summarizes collected data so nurses and local leaders can plan effective programs to solve identified health problems. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h5)

question: What is a major reason why quacks and illegal clinics are still able to operate in some communities?

options.A: Inadequate funding and a shortage of regulatory inspectors

question: What is one of the biggest duties of a community health nurse when dealing with NCDs?

options.A: Manufacturing affordable insulin and blood pressure drugs in local clinics
options.B: Performing major neurosurgeries in rural primary health centers
options.C: Bridging the gap between formal health facilities and grassroots populations
options.D: Enforcing strict national prison sentences for people who eat junk food

explanation: Spot on! Community nurses take health education, screenings, and support right to the doorsteps and neighborhoods where people live. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h6)

question: If a nurse researcher tests patients with a pain scale twice, why is a very short time interval between tests sometimes a bad idea?

options.A: The patients will experience severe physical exhaustion
options.B: Hospital management will not approve the extra paperwork
options.C: Patients might remember and repeat their previous answers
options.D: The thermometer or scale will lose its electrical charge

explanation: This is called recall bias! If patients just remember what they wrote five minutes ago, they'll copy it, making the tool look more reliable than it actually is. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h3)

question: What is the safest tool for a nurse to use when measuring liquid medicine for an infant?

options.A: A regular dining cup
options.B: A standard kitchen teaspoon
options.C: A calibrated oral syringe
options.D: An intravenous syringe

explanation: Household spoons vary wildly in size! A calibrated oral syringe gives us the exact, pinpoint accuracy needed to keep tiny babies safe. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T4#GNS125_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the main goal of conducting regular stock audits on your ward?

options.A: To punish nurses who make simple documentation mistakes
options.B: To verify physical counts against records and ensure accountability
options.C: To remove all medical equipment from the clinical floor
options.D: To increase the purchase price of incoming medications

explanation: Audits aren't there to scare you! They help match what is actually on the shelf with your records, keeping everyone accountable and catching shortages early. [learn more](GST321_U4_T2#GST321_U4_T2_h7)

question: What is the main goal of a computer network in a hospital?

options.A: To permanently replace the need for physical nursing assessment notes
options.B: To supply continuous electrical power during a total blackout
options.C: To increase the processing speed of the central processing unit
options.D: To connect devices so they can share information and resources

explanation: Networks link different computers together so departments can easily talk to each other and share patient updates. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which quality of a study means that if you repeat it, you will get consistent results?

options.A: Reliability
options.B: Neutrality
options.C: Generalizability
options.D: Randomization

explanation: Spot on! Reliability means your tools and methods are dependable and give consistent answers every time. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T2#GNS224_U1_T2_h5)

question: How do out-of-pocket purchases by patients for basic ward supplies affect hospital records?

options.A: They distort standard cost calculations because items are bought outside the system
options.B: They guarantee that all indirect costs are fully covered by the government
options.C: They make hospital accounting completely automatic and error-free
options.D: They eliminate the need for patient classification systems

explanation: When patients run out to buy their own routine supplies, the hospital's official records miss the true picture of what delivering care actually costs. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is it dangerous to start a health program without doing a situation analysis first?

options.A: Community members will refuse to ever speak to healthcare workers
options.B: The government will refuse to disburse salaries to the nursing staff
options.C: Local pharmacy shops will immediately report the clinic to the police
options.D: The program might target problems the community does not consider important

explanation: Skipping situation analysis often leads to wasted resources because interventions fail to address the actual priorities of the local population. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h1)

question: A patient with hypertension insists they stopped adding salt to their food at the table, yet their blood pressure remains high. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: They are drinking too much plain clean water throughout the day
options.B: They are likely consuming hidden sodium from stock cubes, canned fish, and condiments
options.C: They have stopped taking their prescribed medications completely
options.D: They are eating too many fresh, raw fruits from the local market

explanation: Table salt is only part of the intake; hidden sodium in processed seasonings and preserved ingredients can easily ruin a low-salt regimen. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h5)

question: What is an embolus?

options.A: A traveling blood clot or foreign object moving through the bloodstream
options.B: An infection of the outer heart lining
options.C: A normal hole between the right and left atrium
options.D: A sudden widening of the aorta

explanation: An embolus is basically a traveler you don't want! It's any loose mass floating through the blood vessels until it gets stuck in a smaller vessel and blocks the path. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T14#GNS213_U1_T14_h4)

question: Why do extreme crash diets almost always fail in the long run?

options.A: They require professional medical supervision daily
options.B: They cost too much money to purchase ingredients
options.C: They are too restrictive to maintain in daily life
options.D: They contain too many vitamins for the body

explanation: Too true! If a diet is so strict that a patient can't enjoy a normal family meal or local dish, they'll eventually give up. Balance always wins over extreme rules. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h3)

question: What is the recommended feeding approach for a healthy infant under six months old?

options.A: Cow milk mixed with cereal in a baby bottle
options.B: Daily introduction of mashed solid family meals
options.C: Pureed vegetables combined with fruit juices
options.D: Exclusive breastfeeding or infant formula feeding

explanation: For the first six months of life, breast milk or standard infant formula provides all the necessary nutrients and hydration. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h4)

question: Why is disease surveillance compared to an early warning radar?

options.A: It predicts natural disasters like floods that cause water contamination
options.B: It measures the exact wind speed during an airborne disease outbreak
options.C: It helps health workers spot unusual illness clusters before they spread
options.D: It uses satellite technology to track patient movements across borders

explanation: Just like a radar warns of approaching danger, surveillance detects disease spikes early so health teams can respond quickly. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a barrier to good evaluation?

options.A: Resistance to feedback
options.B: Rater bias and halo effects
options.C: Standardized grading rubrics
options.D: Severe time constraints

explanation: Rubrics actually fix evaluation problems by giving clear guidelines so grading is fair and consistent! [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h6)

question: Why is it usually a bad idea to write a research question that can only be answered with a simple 'yes' or 'no'?

options.A: It usually lacks the depth needed to explore complex clinical phenomena
options.B: Ethical boards reject all yes-no questions automatically
options.C: Patients refuse to answer questions with two options
options.D: It is mathematically impossible to analyze yes-no data

explanation: Healthcare is complex! Simple yes/no questions often miss the rich details and depth needed to truly understand patient care. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T8#GNS217_U3_T8_h7)

question: What is a common reason why community members show apathy toward new health programs?

options.A: Excessive amounts of free medicine being supplied
options.B: Past broken promises from government agencies
options.C: Too many nurses wanting to visit the village daily
options.D: Mandatory attendance at international conferences

explanation: Unfulfilled past commitments create cynicism, making residents skeptical of new health initiatives until concrete results are shown. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h6)

question: On a baby's head, what is the area located between the bridge of the nose and the front soft spot called?

options.A: Face
options.B: Occiput
options.C: Brow
options.D: Vertex

explanation: You're doing great! The brow sits right above the eyes and nose. If a baby tries to be born brow-first, it makes for a tricky delivery because that part is quite wide. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h5)

question: In healthcare, what does the term 'pharmacovigilance' mean?

options.A: Monitoring and studying adverse drug reactions and safety issues
options.B: Manufacturing synthetic drugs in sterile laboratory environments
options.C: Setting international market prices for essential pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: Inspecting local pharmacies for expired prescription medications

explanation: Pharmacovigilance simply means keeping a watchful eye on medications to catch, study, and prevent any harmful side effects. You're building great clinical vocabulary! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T2#GNS125_U2_T2_h6)

question: What are early warning signs of a psychiatric relapse?

options.A: Immediate physical healing of a broken bone
options.B: Winning an award at work or school
options.C: Sudden complete recovery and happiness
options.D: Subtle changes like trouble sleeping, irritability, and withdrawing from others

explanation: Early warning signs are small behavioral or emotional shifts that appear before a major crisis occurs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h6)

question: What does a bulging anterior fontanelle usually mean in a newborn?

options.A: Normal developmental closure
options.B: Severe systemic dehydration
options.C: Premature fusion of the skull
options.D: Increased intracranial pressure

explanation: Spot on! Extra pressure inside the head pushes the soft membrane outward, causing that tight, bulging feel. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of follow-up care in mental health?

options.A: To provide ongoing support and monitoring after hospital discharge
options.B: To keep patients admitted in the psychiatric ward indefinitely
options.C: To replace the need for any formal medication or therapy
options.D: To punish patients who do not follow hospital rules

explanation: Follow-up care ensures that patients continue to receive support, check-ups, and monitoring after they leave the hospital setting. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h1)

question: A hospital pharmacy is full of drugs, but the DRF has no cash because an insurance partner is six months late paying claims. What is this called?

options.A: A successful capitation profit
options.B: A cash flow bottleneck
options.C: An operational seed injection
options.D: A complete cost-recovery surplus

explanation: Spot on! When the money is trapped outside the hospital waiting on delayed payments, cash flow gets choked up, leaving you unable to place new orders. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h4)

question: A patient suddenly crashes in the ward, and the nurse in charge immediately takes control and gives clear, fast orders to everyone. What leadership style is this?

options.A: Democratic
options.B: Laissez-faire
options.C: Servant
options.D: Autocratic

explanation: In emergencies, an autocratic style saves lives! It ensures everyone moves fast and coordinates without wasting time debating. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is a major risk if a nurse crosses professional boundaries with a home care patient?

options.A: Improving the patient's physical healing speed instantly
options.B: Eliminating all paperwork requirements for the visit
options.C: Guaranteeing a promotion from the nursing agency
options.D: Compromising clinical objectivity and causing burnout

explanation: Well done! When boundaries get blurry, it's easy to lose your professional focus, which leads to emotional fatigue and can affect the quality of your care. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T4#GNS324_U2_T4_h3)

question: How can Nigerian nurses break through barriers that keep them out of health planning rooms?

options.A: By ignoring hospital management and making independent laws
options.B: By working entirely in private clinics without government oversight
options.C: By building strong professional advocacy and gaining leadership training
options.D: By refusing to care for patients until they are given management titles

explanation: Brilliant! Standing up for our profession, sharpening our leadership skills, and bringing solid evidence helps us earn our rightful seat at the table. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h8)

question: What was the main idea behind the moral treatment movement?

options.A: Spiritual exorcism is the only permanent cure for psychological distress
options.B: Medication is the sole effective intervention for mental disorders
options.C: Patients require strict physical restraint to prevent violent outbursts
options.D: Mental illness should be met with kindness, patience, and a peaceful environment

explanation: Moral treatment tossed out cruelty and punishment. Instead, it focused on human dignity, fresh air, useful activities, and gentle care from staff. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why are elderly patients much more likely to get seriously dehydrated than younger adults?

options.A: They consume strictly dry foods with zero moisture content
options.B: Their kidneys completely stop producing urine as they age
options.C: They often have a reduced sense of thirst and less total body water reserve
options.D: Their skin absorbs environmental moisture instead of retaining internal fluids

explanation: Spot on! As people age, their natural feeling of thirst gets weaker, and they hold less water in their bodies, so they can dry out before they even realize they are thirsty. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h4)

question: What is a key nursing duty when checking a pregnant patient's skin?

options.A: Differentiating harmless body changes from serious medical conditions
options.B: Telling the patient to ignore any skin changes until after delivery
options.C: Reporting all common stretch marks to the primary surgeon
options.D: Prescribing strong steroid creams to cure all rashes instantly

explanation: You are the frontline! Knowing the difference between normal pregnancy glow-ups and warning signs like cholestasis makes you an awesome nurse. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h7)

question: According to the WHO moments for hand hygiene, when is Moment 5?

options.A: Immediately before making physical contact with the patient
options.B: After accidentally touching spilled blood on the floor
options.C: After touching inanimate objects in the patient's immediate surroundings
options.D: Before performing a sterile dressing change

explanation: Moment 5 is all about cleaning your hands after touching things around the patient, like adjusting the bed rail or bedside table. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT something educators look at when choosing your learning experiences?

options.A: The number of students enrolled in the nursing class
options.B: The legal policies and guidelines of the clinical placement agency
options.C: The personal fashion preferences of the nursing students
options.D: The availability of functional skills laboratories and equipment

explanation: Your wardrobe choices don't drive the curriculum! Resource availability, class size, and hospital rules do. [learn more](GST321_U8_T5#GST321_U8_T5_h5)

question: What is the main reason we do nursing research?

options.A: To replace clinical judgement with computer software
options.B: To lower hospital operational costs for management
options.C: To gather evidence and improve patient care
options.D: To reduce the number of working hours in a ward

explanation: You got this! Nursing research is all about finding out what works best so we can give our patients the highest quality of care possible. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T2#GNS224_U1_T2_h1)

question: In holistic palliative care, who is considered the 'unit of care'?

options.A: The patient and their family combined
options.B: Only the patient experiencing the symptoms
options.C: The attending physician and senior nurse
options.D: The immediate hospital nursing ward team

explanation: Think of it this way: an illness affects everyone in the household, so we care for both the patient and their loved ones as a team. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T4#GNS321_U4_T4_h2)

question: What does the term 'deprescribing' mean in clinical practice?

options.A: Writing a brand new prescription after a patient loses their drug chart
options.B: Increasing the dosage strength of a drug to make it work much faster
options.C: Switching a patient from tablets to intravenous injections in the ward
options.D: The planned, supervised process of stopping or reducing unnecessary medications

explanation: Deprescribing isn't abandoning a patient—it's a clever, safe way to trim down unnecessary pills and reduce side effects under medical guidance. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T9#GNS215_U1_T9_h5)

question: How often should you change a clean, intact transparent IV dressing?

options.A: Every 24 hours
options.B: Every 7 days
options.C: Only when the IV line is removed
options.D: Every 14 days

explanation: Standard hospital guidelines recommend changing transparent peripheral IV dressings every 7 days unless they get dirty, loose, or wet. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h5)

question: A patient has widespread body pain, tender points, and ongoing fatigue, but no visible joint swelling. What condition fits best?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Osteoarthritis
options.C: Fibromyalgia
options.D: Gout

explanation: Fibromyalgia is known for widespread pain and tender points, but unlike arthritis, it doesn't cause joint swelling or deformity. Great to keep this distinction in mind! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h3)

question: Why is the variable region of an antibody so important?

options.A: It allows the body to recognize many different antigens
options.B: It provides the structural strength to hold the Y shape
options.C: It helps the antibody attach to normal red blood cells
options.D: It dissolves the cell wall of invading bacteria directly

explanation: Because our bodies face countless different germs, the variable region acts like a shape-shifter at the tips of the antibody, creating diverse binding sites to lock onto various invaders. [learn more](GST114_U4_T3#GST114_U4_T3_h2)

question: Nursing mothers refuse to eat iron-rich organ meats because of a local cultural taboo. What is the best first step for a nurse?

options.A: Identify alternative culturally accepted foods that provide similar iron content
options.B: Tell the mothers their cultural beliefs are completely wrong and unscientific
options.C: Report the mothers to hospital authorities for refusing standard medical advice
options.D: Force-feed the organ meats to ensure the mothers meet daily iron targets

explanation: Great nursing is about teamwork! Instead of fighting tradition, help them find other foods they *are* allowed to eat that give them the same iron. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T027#GNS227_U2_T027_h5)

question: When taking a drug history from a patient in a Nigerian hospital, what must you make sure to ask about?

options.A: Focusing solely on medications taken in the last 24 hours
options.B: Asking only about expensive brand-name medications
options.C: Including traditional herbs and over-the-counter remedies
options.D: Recording only the drugs prescribed by the current hospital

explanation: Many patients take local herbs and chemist drugs alongside hospital meds. Asking about them helps prevent dangerous drug clashes! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T5#GNS215_U2_T5_h5)

question: When do you need to add Transmission-Based Precautions?

options.A: When a specific infection is known or suspected
options.B: When the nurse starts a new morning shift
options.C: When standard handwashing fails to work
options.D: When the patient requests a private room

explanation: You add these special precautions (like gowns or masks) on top of standard ones whenever you're dealing with a specific germ. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h3)

question: Which hormone is mostly linked to the growth of cervical polyps?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Cortisol

explanation: Estrogen is the main driver here! Higher levels can stimulate the cervical lining to overgrow and form a polyp. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h2)

question: What should you do if you notice a clinical policy on your ward is outdated or confusing?

options.A: Change the national health laws to match personal preference
options.B: Report the gap through official institutional channels
options.C: Throw away all printed copies of the hospital rulebook
options.D: Keep the information secret from all other staff members

explanation: Using official reporting channels helps management fix and update policies safely without encouraging risky shortcuts on the ward. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a primary goal of pharmacovigilance?

options.A: Minimizing risks associated with pharmaceutical products
options.B: Promoting the safe and rational use of medicines
options.C: Guarantees that a marketed drug will never cause any side effects
options.D: Contributing to the assessment of drug benefits and harms

explanation: You got it! No drug system can promise zero side effects because all strong medicines carry some level of risk. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why is a physical head-to-toe check important during a nutrition assessment?

options.A: It calculates the precise daily caloric expenditure during rest
options.B: It reveals visible deficiency signs like swollen gums or pale skin
options.C: It replaces the need for laboratory blood tests and dietary records
options.D: It accurately measures the exact percentage of body water volume

explanation: By simply looking at a patient's hair, skin, eyes, and mouth, you can often spot early physical clues of missing vitamins and minerals. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h7)

question: If a primary health care nurse sends a patient to see a mental health specialist, what is this action called?

options.A: Making a referral
options.B: Conducting active listening
options.C: Setting educational goals
options.D: Providing guidance

explanation: When a patient needs specialized care beyond general nursing, connecting them to an expert is called making a referral. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h7)

question: Who stays ultimately responsible for public health when a government enters into a healthcare PPP?

options.A: The private contracting company
options.B: The international donor organizations
options.C: The government health agency
options.D: The individual hospital nursing directors

explanation: Even if private companies help run things, the government remains the main captain and holds the legal and moral duty for the public's health. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h1)

question: How does a situation analysis help with resource allocation?

options.A: By allowing private clinics to buy government drugs cheaply
options.B: By ensuring every single village gets the exact same amount of money
options.C: By hiding medical supplies from the Ministry of Health
options.D: By directing scarce supplies to areas with the greatest need

explanation: Because health resources are always limited, data from a situation analysis ensures supplies go where disease burdens are highest. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h2)

question: A researcher studies teen smoking by surveying a new group of 15-year-olds every year for a decade. Which design is this?

options.A: Panel study
options.B: Randomized controlled trial
options.C: Case-control study
options.D: Trend study

explanation: Spot on! When you sample different individuals from the same population at different times to look for general shifts, it's a trend study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T11#GNS224_U1_T11_h2)

question: Which area of health education focuses on workplace safety and protective gear for workers?

options.A: Maternal and child health
options.B: School health
options.C: Geriatric health
options.D: Occupational health

explanation: Occupational health targets workers in factories, offices, or farms to prevent job-related injuries and illnesses. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h4)

question: Do retrospective studies that only use old patient charts still need ethical approval?

options.A: No, because the patients have already been discharged
options.B: Only if the study is funded by a pharmaceutical company
options.C: Yes, approval from an ethics committee or IRB is still required
options.D: Only if more than one thousand charts are reviewed

explanation: Spot on! Even though the patients aren't actively in the hospital anymore, their health information is still private and protected, so ethical clearance is a must. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T14#GNS224_U1_T14_h6)

question: A community health nurse is assigned to a quarantine camp. Which combination of tasks forms her core daily responsibility?

options.A: Enforcing court orders, arresting rulebreakers, and guarding the perimeter gate
options.B: Importing medical equipment and managing the national budget
options.C: Diagnosing new viral strains using advanced laboratory genome sequencing
options.D: Monitoring temperatures, providing health education, and offering emotional support

explanation: The nurse's core role centers on clinical monitoring, patient education, and psychosocial care within the facility. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h9)

question: What is the highest and broadest level in biological classification?

options.A: Domain
options.B: Family
options.C: Species
options.D: Genus

explanation: The 'Domain' is the topmost level that sorts all cellular life into massive groups: Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya. You've got this! [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which vitamin is especially important for building collagen during long-term wound healing?

options.A: Vitamin B12
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin D

explanation: You nailed it! Vitamin C is key for making collagen, which acts like glue to heal surgical cuts. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h7)

question: What is the primary clinical use of a weighing scale in routine nursing care?

options.A: Assessing nutritional status and tracking fluid balance
options.B: Determining skeletal bone density
options.C: Calculating the total daily calorie intake
options.D: Measuring internal body temperature changes

explanation: Weight measurements help nurses monitor nutritional health and detect sudden fluid shifts in patients. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h1)

question: What is the main way condoms stop pregnancy from happening?

options.A: By thickening cervical mucus permanently
options.B: By stopping ovulation in the ovaries
options.C: By trapping semen to keep sperm out of the uterus
options.D: By killing sperm cells inside the testes

explanation: Exactly right! Condoms act as a physical shield that catches semen so the sperm cannot swim up into the reproductive tract. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h3)

question: What is the biggest hurdle nurses face when handling emergency deliveries in rural community clinics?

options.A: An excessive number of available medical doctors on site
options.B: Lack of immediate access to specialized surgical care and blood banks
options.C: Patients refusing to take prescribed oral medications
options.D: Strict hospital policies preventing any intervention

explanation: Rural clinics often lack advanced surgery and blood supplies, making quick stabilization and fast transfer super important to save lives! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h1)

question: What is a dangerous myth about herbal remedies?

options.A: Some patients experience unexpected side effects from herbs
options.B: Natural plants are completely safe because they come from the earth
options.C: Herbs can interact chemically with prescription psychiatric drugs
options.D: Phytotherapy requires careful dosing supervision by a trained provider

explanation: Just because something is natural doesn't mean it's harmless! Herbs have powerful active chemicals that can react badly with other medicines. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T3#GNS314_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which of the following describes colony morphology?

options.A: Measuring the exact temperature inside a laboratory incubator
options.B: Weighing a glass beaker before adding liquid nutrient broth
options.C: Observing the color and shape of a microbial colony on an agar plate
options.D: Counting the number of student desks in a microbiology classroom

explanation: Spot on! Colony morphology is simply looking at the physical traits of a bacterial colony, like its color, texture, and shape. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h6)

question: What is 'alert fatigue' in a clinical environment?

options.A: Slow loading times when opening multiple patient charts at once
options.B: Physical exhaustion from standing too long at the nursing computer station
options.C: Battery failure in wireless mobile computer carts during a night shift
options.D: Desensitization to warnings caused by too many unimportant pop-up alerts

explanation: Spot on! When software constantly cries wolf with trivial pop-ups, nurses get tired of them and start ignoring all warnings—even the life-saving ones. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why should a patient stay sitting upright for about 30 minutes after eating?

options.A: To allow the nurse enough time to clear the bedside table
options.B: To prevent food reflux and reduce the risk of aspiration
options.C: To encourage the patient to fall into a deep sleep
options.D: To help the digestive enzymes break down fats faster

explanation: Staying upright gives the stomach a head start on digesting, stopping food or acid from creeping back up into the throat. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T3#GNS212_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary design feature of a Shakir tape used in child health?

options.A: It has built-in electronic Bluetooth sensors
options.B: It uses color-coded zones to screen for malnutrition
options.C: It is made of stretchy elastic for comfortable fitting
options.D: It measures body height instead of limb circumference

explanation: Shakir tapes use red, yellow, and green zones so healthcare workers can instantly spot wasting and malnutrition. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h2)

question: How is a research hypothesis different from a research question?

options.A: A hypothesis is always written in the form of a question
options.B: A research question contains independent variables only
options.C: A hypothesis is a declarative statement of predicted outcome
options.D: A research question can never be tested statistically

explanation: Questions ask what might happen, but hypotheses make a bold, clear statement of what you predict the results will be. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T10#GNS217_U3_T10_h6)

question: How does preventing a hospital-acquired infection help save money?

options.A: It shortens hospital stays and reduces extra treatment costs
options.B: It allows the hospital to fire half of its clinical staff
options.C: It completely eliminates all indirect overhead expenses
options.D: It shifts patient care expenses entirely to the government

explanation: Preventing complications saves money naturally because patients get well faster, needing fewer drugs, fewer tests, and shorter bed days. [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why is a functional assessment necessary when caring for someone with a physical disability?

options.A: To prove that the patient is unable to walk
options.B: To diagnose the original cause of the injury
options.C: To determine the financial cost of hospital equipment
options.D: To match nursing interventions with the patient's actual capabilities

explanation: Assessing what a patient can still do prevents nurses from doing tasks the patient is fully capable of managing themselves. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h1)

question: What is widely considered the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in a hospital?

options.A: Wearing heavy utility gloves all day
options.B: Spraying chemical disinfectants on walls
options.C: Keeping all windows wide open
options.D: Consistent and proper hand hygiene

explanation: Good old handwashing (or using an alcohol rub) is your superpower. It stops germs dead in their tracks before they reach you or your next patient. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h6)

question: Why must a nurse be culturally sensitive when talking about traditional health practices in a rural area?

options.A: It proves that traditional beliefs are always scientifically accurate
options.B: It builds trust and encourages the community to accept safer health practices
options.C: It ensures the nurse receives financial grants from foreign donors
options.D: It prevents the government from closing down the local health post

explanation: Respect opens doors! When you honor people's culture, they trust you enough to listen when you introduce safer health habits. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T9#GNS122_U3_T9_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of 'controlling' in healthcare management?

options.A: Hiring new nursing graduates for vacancies
options.B: Monitoring performance to ensure care matches established standards
options.C: Assigning daily cleaning duties to support staff
options.D: Creating the holiday duty roster

explanation: Controlling means checking how things are going so you can maintain high standards of patient care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h6)

question: A 25-year-old male client reports finding a hard, painless lump in his left testicle. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Prostate adenocarcinoma
options.B: Testicular cancer
options.C: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.D: Renal cell carcinoma

explanation: Testicular cancer is most commonly seen in young adult men. A painless lump or swelling in the scrotum should always be checked out right away. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h4)

question: What is the main difference between being 'gifted' and having a 'talent'?

options.A: Giftedness is general mental potential while talent is specific performance.
options.B: Talent appears in early childhood whereas giftedness appears in adolescence.
options.C: Giftedness relies on physical skill while talent relies on memory.
options.D: Talent requires formal testing whereas giftedness develops naturally.

explanation: You've got this! Think of giftedness as a broad, overall high intellectual ability, while talent is when someone shines brightly in one specific area, like music or math. Keep going! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T1#GNS225_U5_T1_h1)

question: Why do teenage girls need more dietary iron than young boys of the same age?

options.A: To replace iron lost monthly through menstruation
options.B: To compensate for low carbohydrate intake
options.C: To prevent the rapid onset of adult diabetes
options.D: To build stronger tooth enamel

explanation: That's correct! Regular menstrual blood loss means teenage girls need extra iron in their diet to stay energetic and avoid anemia. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h3)

question: Why don't people usually have severe allergic reactions the very first time they meet a new trigger?

options.A: The body needs time to first build up and sensitize IgE antibodies to that trigger.
options.B: Allergens can only enter the bloodstream after the skin has been damaged twice.
options.C: The immune system is completely dormant until the third or fourth exposure occurs.
options.D: First exposures are always destroyed completely by normal white blood cells in the liver.

explanation: You got it! The first exposure acts as a rehearsal—it primes your immune system by creating those special IgE antibodies, which then react fiercely the *next* time you meet the trigger. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T8#GNS215_U6_T8_h1)
